pages: Neural networks learn patterns from examples. They adjust many numbers, called weights, so that their outputs get closer to the answers in the training data! Does more data always help? Not always: noisy labels can hurt, as shown by Smith et al. in Fig. 3. A held-out test set estimates how the model behaves on unseen cases. Researchers therefore never tune on it. Short one.
